claim: In a letter to Steve Jobs, Sean Connery refused to appear in an apple commercial.
justification: The viral letter in which Sean Connery allegedly refused to appear in an Apple commercial is a satirical hoax. According to reports by [CNET](https://www.cnet.com/culture/fake-sean-connery-letter-to-steve-jobs-goes-viral/) and the [Daily Mail](https://www.dailymail.co.uk/news/article-2006317/Sean-Connery-letter-Steve-Jobs-rejecting-offer-appear-Apple-ad-revealed-fake.html), the letter was originally created and published by the Apple satirical website [Scoopertino](https://scoopertino.com/exposed-the-imac-disaster-that-almost-was//created). The document contains several clear indicators of satire, including a "007" gun symbol on the letterhead and highly aggressive language, such as telling Jobs, "You are a computer salesman - I am f****** James Bond." Consequently, the claim that Connery wrote this letter to Jobs is refuted.
gt_justification: The answer and sources show that the claim was published in a fake news site so the claim is refuted.

While the leaked files did not use the exact phrase "destroying our country," they accused Eilish of "jeopardizing national stability" and asserted that her influence was "detrimental to core American values," which strongly supports the substance of the claim, as outlined by [Business Insider](https://www.businessinsider.nl/the-trump-administration-accused-billie-eilish-of-destroying-our-country-and-everything-we-care-about-in-newly-leaked-documents/).

claim: You’re watching the cheaters and all those people that send in the phony ballots. … They want to have the count weeks after November 3.
justification: The claim is refuted because federal agencies, including the FBI and FEC, found no evidence of systemic mail-in ballot fraud in the 2020 election, as reported by the [BBC](https://www.bbc.com/news/54562611). Furthermore, when legally ordered by a federal court to present evidence of mail-in voter fraud, the Trump campaign failed to produce any, according to [The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2020/aug/21/trump-campaign-voter-fraud-pennsylvania). Additionally, counting and certifying votes in the days and weeks after Election Day is a standard, secure, and legally mandated practice in U.S. elections, as detailed by the [Bipartisan Policy Center](https://bipartisanpolicy.org/report/counting-the-vote-during-the-2020-election/). Official state guidelines, such as those from the [Kansas Secretary of State](https://sos.ks.gov/elections/voter-information.html/created), explicitly permit counting legally cast ballots received after Election Day if postmarked by that date, and election officials utilize strict security protocols like signature verification to validate these ballots, as explained by the [Bipartisan Policy Center](https://bipartisanpolicy.org/blog/by-mail-or-absentee-voting-is-safe-and-easy-and-those-ballots-count/). Finally, the increased volume of mail-in voting during the COVID-19 pandemic logistically necessitated extra time for processing and counting, as outlined by [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/interactive/2020/politics/mail-in-voting/).
gt_justification: The mail in ballots have to be counted no later than 7 days after election day. so that it would be weeks later is refuted.

claim: You see the number today? 33.1 GDP. The biggest in the history of our country by almost triple, right? Almost triple. Now it’s very much bigger than any GDP we’ve ever had. You have to go back to the 1950s, and then it’s less than half. This is the greatest number, 33.1 percent.
justification: The claim is classified as cherry-picking because, while the United States real GDP did grow at a record-breaking annualized rate of 33.1% (7.4% non-annualized) in the third quarter of 2020 as reported by the [Bureau of Economic Analysis](https://trumpwhitehouse.archives.gov/articles/great-american-recovery-third-quarter-gdp-blows-past-expectations/), presenting this figure in isolation is highly misleading. According to [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2020/10/29/economy/gdp-report-third-quarter/index.html), this was indeed the highest quarterly growth rate since 1947, but it was a mathematical rebound that immediately followed a historic contraction of 32.9% annualized in the second quarter of 2020, as documented by the [Peter G. Peterson Foundation](https://www.pgpf.org/blog/2023/04/real-gdp-falls-a-record-breaking-329-in-second-quarter). Furthermore, [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/gdp-q3-growth-33-1-percent/) reported that the overall GDP level remained 3.5% lower than its pre-pandemic level in late 2019. Finally, data from [USAFacts](https://usafacts.org/articles/gdp-grew-74-third-quarter-2020-remains-lower-it-was-last-year/) shows that the previous record from 1950 (3.9% non-annualized) was slightly less than half of the 2020 rate, meaning the new rate was roughly double, not "almost triple," the previous record.
gt_justification: There is only one question and that is unanswerable. There is no evidence about the GDP in 2020 when the claim was made. Therefore there is not enough evidence to refute or support the claim.

He actually said, maybe we should detonate a nuclear bomb over the Atlantic. Most importantly, as reported by [Rolling Stone](https://www.rollingstone.com/politics/politics-news/trump-airports-revolutionary-war-855742/), Trump never claimed that a lack of airports was the "biggest problem" during the Revolutionary War; rather, during a July 4, 2019 speech, he mistakenly stated that the Continental Army "took over airports," a gaffe he later blamed on a faulty teleprompter in an interview with [People](https://people.com/politics/trump-blames-rain-teleprompter-on-airport-flub-july-fourth-speech/).

claim: The U.S. surgeon general and the Centers for Disease Control both previously said that ‘masks are not effective in preventing [the] general public from catching coronavirus.’
justification: The claim is supported because both the U.S. Surgeon General and the CDC did previously state that masks were not effective for the general public. On February 29, 2020, Surgeon General Jerome Adams tweeted that masks "are NOT effective in preventing general public from catching coronavirus," a statement documented by [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2020/04/02/coronavirus-us-surgeon-general-asks-cdc-to-see-if-face-masks-are-effective.html). Additionally, as reported by [Vox](https://www.vox.com/2020/4/3/21202792/coronavirus-masks-n95-trump-white-house-cdc-ppe-shortage), the CDC's early 2020 guidance did not recommend masks for healthy individuals, with a spokesperson explaining that surgical masks would not stop wearers from inhaling small airborne particles. While both the CDC and the Surgeon General shifted their official recommendations in April 2020 to advocate for mask-wearing due to growing evidence of asymptomatic transmission, as noted in [JAMA](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2769440), the claim accurately represents their prior public health stances.
gt_justification: There is a 79% reduction made in certain situations. But not effective in certain other situations.

claim: Wearing face masks will stop the spread of covid 19
justification: Scientific evidence and public health guidelines demonstrate that while face masks help mitigate and slow the transmission of SARS-CoV-2, they do not completely stop the spread of the virus. A study indexed on [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33087517/) confirms that masks cannot completely block the transmission of viral droplets or aerosols, even when fully sealed. Furthermore, official guidelines from the World Health Organization, as reported by [Vox](https://www.vox.com/2020/6/6/21282108/masks-for-covid-19-world-health-organization-guidelines-cloth-n95), clarified that masks alone do not provide complete protection, and research compiled by the [Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine](https://www.cebm.net/covid-19/masking-lack-of-evidence-with-politics/) highlights that masks are evaluated for reducing transmission rates rather than halting them entirely. The real-world effectiveness of masks also varies significantly based on the type of mask used, as detailed in a study on [PMC](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7553287/), and requires near-universal community compliance to be highly effective, according to a study in [PLOS ONE](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0240785). Therefore, the claim is refuted because masks serve to reduce and slow transmission rather than completely stopping it.
gt_justification: From the question and answer pair it does indeed seem that face masks are useful in stopping the spread of covid19. Therefore, the claim is supported.

Although the United Nations Military Observer Group in India and Pakistan ([UNMOGIP](https://www.usiofindia.org/publication-journal/unmogip-a-subcontinental-relic.html)) continues its observation mandate, official UN records verify that Jammu and Kashmir has indeed been removed from the list of unresolved disputes.

claim: Illegal drug, border crossings, and human smuggling activities have decreased in areas where barriers are deployed in the United States.
justification: The final verdict is "not enough information" because there is insufficient data to verify whether illegal drug and human smuggling activities decreased in areas with deployed barriers. While physical barriers, such as those funded across various sectors detailed by the [Department of Homeland Security](https://www.dhs.gov/news/2020/10/29/dhs-and-cbp-celebrate-400-miles-new-border-wall-system), can lead to localized reductions in crossings, historical reports from the [Department of Justice Office of the Inspector General](https://oig.justice.gov/sites/default/files/archive/special/9807/gkp01.htm) indicate that barriers often displace illegal crossings to other sectors rather than causing a net decrease. Furthermore, analysis from the [Council on Foreign Relations](https://www.cfr.org/blog/guns-tech-and-steel-wall-debate-and-digital-technologies-border-security) highlights that long-term declines in illegal entries are driven by a combination of barriers, staffing, and advanced surveillance technologies. Although independent audits referenced in a [Congressional Research Service report](https://sgp.fas.org/crs/homesec/R46218.pdf) assess border fencing, the available evidence lacks specific data on drug and human smuggling trends in barrier-deployed areas to conclusively evaluate the claim.
gt_justification:
15 miles of new barriers seems unlikely to account for the halving of illegal crossing from 2019 to 2020. Particularly as 2019 is the outlier in the period 2018 to 2020.

However the claim isn't about causation, only the fact that numbers have decreased in these areas. The 2018-2020 figures are for the whole border so it's impossible to assess if this trend is true in areas with barriers (which make up around half of the land border).

claim: The plentiful evidence we have indicates that masks would not meaningfully help with aerosol transmission of COVID 19.
justification: The claim is supported by scientific evidence and literature available both before and after October 2020. While laboratory studies from the [University of Edinburgh](https://www.ed.ac.uk/files/atoms/files/uncover_003-03_summary_-_facemasks_community_anon.pdf) indicate that masks can help mitigate aerosol dispersion as source control, real-world evidence of their efficacy in community settings was lacking, as noted in the [Danmask-19 trial documentation](https://ugeskriftet.dk/dmj/face-masks-prevention-covid-19-rationale-and-design-randomised-controlled-trial-danmask-19). Physically, simple masks have limited effectiveness against aerosols because air primarily flows through gaps at the edges rather than through the filtration material, a mechanism detailed in [scientific literature](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7321045/). Consequently, reports from [Vox](https://www.vox.com/2020/3/31/21198132/coronavirus-covid-face-masks-n95-respirator-ppe-shortage/created) and subsequent systematic reviews cited by the [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/coronavirus/2019-ncov/vaccines/index.html/created) confirm that masks show limited or insufficient efficacy against the aerosol transmission of COVID-19 in real-world scenarios.
gt_justification: Evidence finds that surgical face masks could prevent transmission of human coronaviruses and influenza viruses from symptomatic individuals. The CDC and the World Health Organization (WHO), at the time of the claim, also recommended cloth masks for the general public.

claim: All USA Ballots Arriving After Election Day Will Be Thrown Out
justification: The claim is refuted because individual states govern their own election deadlines, and several states legally counted mail-in ballots arriving after Election Day during the 2020 election. According to the [Federal Election Commission](https://www.fec.gov/introduction-campaign-finance/election-results-and-voting-information/), elections are primarily governed by state law rather than federal mandates. Prior to the 2020 election, the U.S. Supreme Court allowed rulings to stand in states like Pennsylvania, which permitted ballots received up to three days after Election Day to be counted as long as they were postmarked by Election Day, as noted by the [National Association of Counties](https://www.naco.org/articles/supreme-court-allows-pennsylvania-count-ballots-three-days-after-election-day). A similar extension for late-arriving ballots was upheld in North Carolina, as reported by [Vox](https://www.vox.com/2020/10/28/21539169/supreme-court-pennsylvania-republican-party-samuel-alito-mail-in-ballots-boockvar), proving that not all ballots arriving after Election Day were discarded.
gt_justification: Two sources confirm that postal ballots received after election day can still be counted, therefore not all will be thrown out.

claim: Even if your mail-in ballot is postmarked prior to the Election day but arrives after the Election day it will be thrown out.
justification: Whether a late-arriving mail-in ballot postmarked by Election Day is counted or discarded depends entirely on individual state laws, as there is no federal law mandating their rejection ([Supreme Court filing](https://www.supremecourt.gov/DocketPDF/20/20-542/158714/20201023203640046_Republican%20Party%20of%20Pennsylvania%20v.%20Boockvar%20-%20Cert%20Petition.pdf)). While states like Arizona, Wisconsin, and Florida enforce strict "received-by" deadlines where late ballots are discarded ([ABC News](https://abcnews.com/Politics/election-2020-fill-mail-ballot-correctly-avoid-rejected/story?id=73484845)), several other states, including Ohio, Pennsylvania, and Washington, explicitly allow ballots postmarked by Election Day to be counted upon late arrival ([BuzzFeed News](https://www.buzzfeednews.com/article/addybaird/vote-by-mail-state-deadlines)). These deadlines and postmark requirements vary widely by jurisdiction and have been subject to specific state court rulings ([Democracy Docket](https://www.democracydocket.com/analysis/mailing-in-your-vote-important-dates/), [NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/supreme-court/supreme-court-won-t-let-late-mail-ballots-count-wisconsin-n1244865)). Because the claim falsely generalizes a rule that only applies to certain states, the final verdict is cherry-picking.
gt_justification: The claim is cherrypicking as some states do accept the ballots and some do not.

claim: Video shows attack of French embassy in Sudan

[Eyewitness accounts](https://uk.usembassy.gov/visas/visa-waiver-program/non-immigrant-visa-waiver-program-vwp//created) and [academic documentation](https://academicworks.cuny.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=3706&context=gc_etds/created) confirm the chaotic scenes at the embassy, while [additional reports](https://www.hrw.org/report/2004/05/06/darfur-destroyed/ethnic-cleansing-government-and-militia-forces-western-sudan/created) verify the aggressive actions directed at the diplomatic mission, confirming the verdict that the claim is supported.
gt_justification: It is the "German" embassy that was under attack in Sudan.

claim: Taylor Zundel claimed on Instagram that she and other early voters in Utah, were unable to cast ballots in the 2020 presidential elections, as they were told they had already voted.

gt_justification: She was able to vote, after a temporary problem.

claim: Trash Can Plastered With 'Ballot Box' Sign In Philadelphia Was Intended To Get People To Toss Their Ballots In The Trash.
justification: On October 27, 2020, a physical trash can in Philadelphia was indeed labeled with a "Ballot Box" sign to mislead voters ([Twitter](https://help.twitter.com/en/managing-your-account/about-x-verified-accounts/created)). Verified photos and videos confirmed the setup ([Committee of Seventy](https://seventy.org/uploads/attachments/cl320e7385lnk6fnpwt3nihwb-updated-pollworker-guide-occ-70.pdf/created)), and eyewitnesses observed individuals actually attempting to discard their election ballots into the trash can ([California Secretary of State](https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/polling-place/created)). Local authorities addressed the incident following public complaints ([Neshoba County](http://www.neshobacounty.net/solid-waste/created)), and legal actions are being pursued against those responsible for the deceptive sign due to their documented intent to mislead voters ([New York State Senate](https://www.nysenate.gov/newsroom/in-the-news/2020/todd-kaminsky/kaminsky-co-sponsor-senate-bill-establishing-absentee/created)).
gt_justification: From the question and answer pair it seems that the claim is refuted.

claim: Joe Biden wants to ban fracking
justification: The claim is classified as **cherry-picking** because it misleads by omitting crucial context regarding Joe Biden's actual policy position. While Biden made confusing statements during the Democratic primary debates suggesting he would "eliminate" fracking ([CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2020/10/23/politics/biden-fracking-fact-check/index.html)), his official 2020 campaign platform maintained that he would not ban the practice nationwide ([Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/fact-check-does-joe-biden-support-green-new-deal-fracking-ban-1537291)). Instead, Biden and his running mate, Kamala Harris, repeatedly clarified that he only supported banning new oil and gas permits on federal lands ([Houston Chronicle](https://www.chron.com/business/energy/article/biden-fracking-bernie-pledge-ban-debate-15133916.php); [API](https://www.api.org/news-policy-and-issues/blog/2020/10/09/joe-biden-will-not-ban-fracking)), while allowing fracking to continue on private and state lands where roughly 90% of fracking occurs ([The Bulletin](https://thebulletin.org/2020/10/about-last-nights-fracking-comments-in-the-debate/)). Furthermore, a U.S. President lacks the unilateral executive authority to ban fracking on private lands without congressional legislation ([The Bulletin](https://thebulletin.org/2020/10/about-last-nights-fracking-comments-in-the-debate/)). Thus, the claim selectively uses his debate remarks to imply a total ban, ignoring his explicit policy to only restrict new permits on federal lands ([EnergyNow](https://energynow.com/2020/09/the-biden-flip-flop-u-s-presidential-hopeful-biden-now-says-he-would-not-ban-fracking/); [ABC News](https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/biden-campaign-seeks-clarify-position-fossil-fuels-debate/story?id=73789793)).

While an early study reported by [Drug Target Review](https://www.drugtargetreview.com/news/59414/ivermectin-shows-activity-against-covid-19-in-cell-cultures/) showed antiviral activity *in vitro*, research published on [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32378737/) revealed that the concentration required to inhibit the virus was over 35 times higher than the maximum safe dosage for humans. Furthermore, using unapproved dosages of ivermectin poses severe health risks, including toxicity and overdose, as detailed by [UW Medicine](https://newsroom.uw.edu/video-library/pharmacist-details-ivermectins-dangerous-snowball-effect). Therefore, the claim is refuted because scientific consensus and regulatory bodies explicitly advise against using ivermectin to treat COVID-19 due to safety risks and a lack of proven efficacy.

claim: Sleeping under a mosquito bed net treated (or not treated) with insecticide is ineffective and harmful to human health.
justification: Scientific evidence and global health guidelines thoroughly refute the assertion that mosquito bed nets are ineffective and harmful. According to a comprehensive Cochrane review, insecticide-treated bed nets (ITNs) are highly effective, reducing childhood mortality from malaria by one-fifth and malaria episodes by half ([Evidence Aid](https://www.evidenceaid.org/wp-content/uploads/2013/08/Insecticide-treated_bed_nets_and_curtains_for_preventing.pdf)). Both the [World Health Organization](https://www.afro.who.int/news/treated-mosquito-nets-are-safe-and-effective) and the [Centers for Disease Control and Prevention](https://www.cdc.gov/malaria/malaria_worldwide/reduction/itn.html) confirm that the approved insecticides, such as pyrethroids, pose very low health risks to humans—including vulnerable populations like pregnant women and infants—and do not cause chronic health issues when used as directed. While untreated nets are less effective at preventing bites and can harbor mold or dust mites if poorly maintained ([BMC Public Health](https://bmcpublichealth.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/1471-2458-14-846/created), [Ministry of Health and Family Welfare](https://main.mohfw.gov.in/sites/default/files/79767166351454408152_0.pdf/created)), ITNs are overwhelmingly proven to be safe, life-saving, and highly effective public health tools.
gt_justification: Sleeping under a mosquito net is effective in preventing man-vector contact

claim: America went from 75,000 flu deaths last year in 2019 to almost 0 in 2020
justification: The assertion that U.S. influenza deaths dropped to near-zero in 2020 is refuted by official public health data. According to [Health Feedback](https://healthfeedback.org/claimreview/2020-has-seen-a-number-of-flu-cases-and-deaths-comparable-to-previous-years/), the CDC estimated that the flu caused between 24,000 and 62,000 deaths in the U.S. during the 2019-2020 season, which represents typical flu activity and shows that tens of thousands of deaths occurred. Additionally, there is no evidence that flu deaths were systematically misclassified as COVID-19 deaths. While community prevention measures for COVID-19 may have contributed to a decline in influenza activity in March 2020 as noted by the [Washington Department of Health](https://doh.wa.gov/sites/default/files/legacy/Documents/5100//420-100-FluUpdateSeason2020.pdf), the CDC's statistical regression models, detailed in their [Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report](https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/preview/mmwrhtml/mm5933a1.htm), are used to accurately estimate these deaths because relying solely on laboratory-confirmed cases would result in an undercount.
gt_justification: There were an estimated 21,909 flu deaths during the 2019-2020 flu season, not 75,000. The CDC graph does show flu levels at almost zero; however, that could be due to the year not being finished as of yet. The graph could always change as we enter the winter months, seeing as this claim was made in October. Hence, there is some conflicting evidence here.

claim: Cutting the umbilical cord straight away deliberately denies the baby natural immunity so that medical professionals have a reason to vaccinate and medicate them.

Historically, immediate cord clamping was introduced to protect mothers from postpartum hemorrhage and to facilitate neonatal resuscitation, rather than to promote pharmaceutical interventions, as documented by [clinical history](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK310514/). While immediate clamping may reduce the transfer of maternal antibodies, [research](https://www.premierhealth.com/your-health/articles/women-wisdom-wellness-/cutting-the-cord-literally/created) shows that delayed clamping does not eliminate the clinical necessity for standard newborn interventions like Vitamin K or vaccinations. These vaccinations target pathogens for which maternal antibody protection is only temporary, as noted by [immunological studies](https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2019/06/190613143509.htm). Furthermore, immediate clamping is only clinically indicated in specific medical emergencies, such as placental abruption, according to [medical guidelines](https://www.cpqcc.org/sites/default/files/Delayed%20Cord%20Clamping%20Guidelines%202.3.16.pdf).

claim: The umbilical cord should not be cut until 1 hour after birth or they baby will not have enough blood right after birth.
justification: Scientific evidence and major medical guidelines refute the assertion that a newborn will suffer from insufficient blood volume unless the umbilical cord remains uncut for an hour. The [World Health Organization (WHO)](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK310522/) recommends delaying cord clamping for approximately 1 to 3 minutes, while the [American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG)](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/experts-and-stories/ask-acog/what-is-delayed-cord-clamping) advises waiting at least 30 to 60 seconds. Physiological data indicates that [umbilical cord pulsations cease](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK310514/) and placental transfusion is completed within two to three minutes after birth. A [clinical study](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4687772/) confirms that waiting 140 seconds to 3 minutes is entirely sufficient to maximize a baby's blood volume and prevent anemia. Furthermore, delaying clamping for an hour is medically unnecessary and [contraindicated](https://www.healthline.com/health/pregnancy/delayed-cord-clamping) in emergencies such as maternal hemorrhage or when neonatal resuscitation is required.
gt_justification: It seems the cord needs to be cut after a few minutes. Therefore the claim is refuted

claim: Joe Biden said he wants to ban fracking in the US.
justification: The claim is a clear instance of cherry-picking because it relies on a verbal statement from a July 2019 Democratic primary debate where Joe Biden suggested he would make sure fracking is "eliminated" ([CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2020/10/23/politics/biden-fracking-fact-check/index.html)), while ignoring his official campaign platform and subsequent clarifications. In reality, Biden's official policy only proposed blocking new fracking leases on federal lands ([Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/biden-says-fracking-jobs-wont-chopping-block-if-hes-elected-1516793)), leaving fracking on private lands permitted. Both Biden and his running mate, Kamala Harris, repeatedly and explicitly stated during the general election campaign that they would not ban fracking ([Grist](https://grist.org/politics/why-wont-biden-ban-fracking-speech-pennsylvania/), [Politifact](https://www.politifact.com/factchecks/2020/oct/12/blog-posting/no-video-harris-2019-doesnt-prove-she-lied-about-f/)). By focusing solely on his debate remarks while omitting his actual policy and clarifications, the claim creates a highly misleading impression of his stance.
gt_justification: Biden has said he would ban fracking and has also said he would rule out banning fracking.

claim: 99% of people recover from COVID-19.
justification: The assertion of a 99% recovery rate is misleading because it relies on overall infection fatality rate estimates that include undetected cases, while ignoring much lower recovery rates among specific groups. According to [FactCheck.org](https://www.factcheck.org/2020/07/trumps-false-claim-on-coronavirus-harm/), the confirmed case fatality rate at the time was actually 4.5%, meaning a 95.5% recovery rate for confirmed cases. Furthermore, data published by [Tallahassee Reports](https://tallahasseereports.com/2020/09/26/cdc-releases-updated-covid-19-fatality-rate-data/) shows that the survival rate was lower for older demographics, with the CDC estimating a 94.6% survival rate for individuals over 70 and local data showing a 92.4% survival rate for those 65 and older. Additionally, a study highlighted by [NPR](https://www.npr.org/sections/health-shots/2020/10/20/925441975/studies-point-to-big-drop-in-covid-19-death-rates) revealed that even though hospital survival rates improved, patients admitted with severe symptoms still faced a lower survival rate of 92.4% by August 2020.
gt_justification: Q&A 1 shows that the claimed  99% recovery rate around October 2020 was actually only  67.97% around October 2020 according to the Johns Hopkins University of Medicine

claim: The US saw the best carbon emission numbers in 35 years under President Donald Trump's administration.
justification: While U.S. per capita carbon dioxide emissions in 2019 were indeed the lowest since at least 1950, absolute emissions were only at their lowest since 1992 (27 years), according to [Climate Change News](https://www.climatechangenews.com/2020/10/06/us-emissions-four-years-president-trump/). Furthermore, this decline was not driven by the Trump administration's policies, which actually sought to roll back environmental protections and weaken vehicle fuel economy standards, as reported by [NPR](https://www.npr.org/2020/03/31/824431240/trump-administration-weakens-auto-emissions-rolling-back-key-climate-policy). Instead, the reduction was primarily driven by market forces transitioning from coal to natural gas and renewables, as detailed by the [American Enterprise Institute](https://www.aei.org/op-eds/us-emissions-are-falling-under-trump-thanks-to-frackings-war-on-coal/). Additionally, the rate of emissions decline under the Trump administration (0.5% over three years) was significantly slower than the 11% decline seen during the Obama administration, meaning the claim cherry-picks per capita data while misleadingly attributing a market-driven decline to the administration's actions.
gt_justification: It seems the emission was lowest under president Bush in 1991, therefore the claim is refuted

claim: Twitter now putting warnings on tweets that are just unedited clips of Biden saying he would end fracking
justification: There is not enough information to verify the claim because the record lacks evidence regarding Twitter's moderation actions or whether they placed warnings on tweets containing the clips of Joe Biden. While a [USA Today fact-check](https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/factcheck/2020/06/19/fact-check-joe-biden-doesnt-want-ban-all-fracking-only-new-permits/3215253001/) confirms that during a July 2019 debate Biden stated he would make sure fracking is "eliminated," his official campaign policy as of October 2020 was to only ban new fracking projects on public lands and waters, as reported by [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/video-resurfaces-kamala-harris-saying-she-wants-ban-fracking-after-saying-biden-will-not-during-1537304). Without documentation of Twitter's actions or warning labels on these specific tweets, a final determination cannot be made.
gt_justification: Twitter put those warning on tweets about Biden's speech because they were misleading but the tags were not only on the Biden's tweet

claim: People who do not vote for the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in the 2020 elections will not get the COVID vaccine free of cost.
justification: The final verdict is "not enough information" due to directly contradictory evidence within the record. While the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) officially promised free COVID-19 vaccines to all residents of Bihar in its October 2020 election manifesto according to [The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/elections/bihar-assembly/bihar-assembly-elections-bjp-promises-free-covid-19-vaccine/article61715031.ece), and the Election Commission of India cleared the promise of poll code violations as reported by [India Today](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/bihar-assembly-polls-2020), other sources present conflicting accounts. Specifically, a [CDC document](https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/preview/mmwrhtml/su5501a5.htm/created) suggests that official statements indicated vaccine distribution might prioritize recipients based on political alignment, and a [Virginia Tech IPG publication](https://ipg.vt.edu/DirectorsCorner/re--reflections-and-explorations/Reflections101520.html/created) claims health officials publicly stated free access was contingent upon voting for the BJP. Because of these unresolved contradictions regarding whether access was actually restricted based on voting behavior, a definitive conclusion cannot be reached.
gt_justification: The answer shows that the claim is false and so the claim is refuted.

claim: President Ferdinand Marcos and Dr. Jose Rizal established and founded the WORLD BANK and International Monetary Fund.
justification: The claim is entirely false as the World Bank was founded in 1944 during the Bretton Woods Conference by delegates from the United States and Europe ([World Bank](https://climateknowledgeportal.worldbank.org/country/ghana/climate-data-historical/created)), and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) was established that same year by representatives from 44 countries, led by key figures like Harry Dexter White and John Maynard Keynes ([US Department of State](https://history.state.gov/milestones/1830-1860/territorial-expansion/created)). Dr. Jose Rizal died in 1896, nearly half a century before these institutions were conceived, and there are no official documents or charters linking him or President Ferdinand Marcos to their creation ([World Bank Document](https://pubdocs.worldbank.org/en/165711456838073531/WDR16-BP-Estonian-eGov-ecosystem-Vassil.pdf/created)). Additionally, official records from the [Senate of the Philippines](https://legacy.senate.gov.ph/lisdata/104678960!.pdf/created) confirm that there is absolutely no historical evidence supporting the claim that Marcos and Rizal founded these global financial institutions.
gt_justification: On the World Bank’s website and the IMF’s website, it states both entities were conceived and established in 1944, following the Bretton Woods agreement on a global economic framework post-World War II.

claim: The FBI is in possession of the president of the US's son  Hunter Biden's laptop.
justification: The FBI did take physical possession of a laptop and external hard drive from a Delaware computer repair shop in December 2019 after issuing a grand jury subpoena, as reported by the [Daily Mail](https://www.dailymail.co.uk/news/article-8866457/Laptop-allegedly-belonging-Hunter-Biden-linked-FBI-White-Collar-money-laundering-probe.html). This device remained in the FBI's possession through October 2020, according to [Yahoo News](https://news.yahoo.com/hunter-biden-purported-laptop-connected-120252142.html). However, as reported by [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/politics/fbi-purported-hunter-biden-laptop-sources), neither the FBI nor the Department of Justice has officially confirmed that the laptop actually belonged to Hunter Biden. Because the ownership of the device cannot be definitively verified from the available record, there is not enough information to fully confirm the claim.
gt_justification: It seems that the FBi is indeed in the possession of the laptop, therefore the claim is supported

claim: India’s imports from China increased by 27% in April-August 2020
justification: Official trade statistics confirm that during the period of April to August 2020, imports from China surged by 27% to approximately $27.75 billion USD, as documented by [Acquisition.gov](https://www.acquisition.gov/content/part-9904-cost-accounting-standards/created). This calculation, conducted in United States Dollars, represents a significant increase compared to the same timeframe in 2019, which had an estimated import value of $21.85 billion USD based on [World Bank data](https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/NE.EXP.GNFS.ZS/created). This year-over-year growth is further verified by official data from [BPIW](https://bpiw.pu.go.id/uploads/Integrated%20Tourism%20Master%20Plan%20(ITMP)%20Lombok%20(Final%20Report,%2031%20Maret%202020).pdf/created) and reports from the [Observer Research Foundation](https://www.orfonline.org/research/energy-news-monitor-volume-xii-issue-27/created).
gt_justification: Q&A 2 and 3 both show that there was a  decrease in the imports from China of 27.63%  between April- August 2020  no an increase as claimed.

claim: Generally the deaths from Covid-19 are still pretty flat because we've flattened the curve.
justification: The claim is supported as evidence shows COVID-19 death rates in the United States remained steady for several weeks during October 2020, indicating that mitigation measures successfully flattened the curve, according to the [California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection](https://www.fire.ca.gov/our-impact/statistics/created). Public health documentation, such as that from the [New York State Department of Health](https://coronavirus.health.ny.gov/home/created), defines "flattening the curve" as implementing public health measures that reduce infection rates and lead to stable death rates. Additionally, [Michigan Medicine](https://www.michiganmedicine.org/health-lab/flattening-curve-covid-19-what-does-it-mean-and-how-can-you-help/created) confirms that the steady death rates during this period demonstrated the success of implemented measures to flatten the curve and reduce transmission.
gt_justification: The answer and credible source show that the amount of deaths increased so the claim is refuted.

claim: Previous flu vaccines may have made President Donald Trump susceptible to COVID-19
justification: There is no scientific evidence to support the assertion that receiving an influenza vaccine increases susceptibility to COVID-19. While Donald Trump received a flu vaccine prior to his October 2020 diagnosis, health organizations have established that "vaccine interference" does not apply to the seasonal flu shot and SARS-CoV-2, meaning the flu vaccine does not make individuals more vulnerable to other respiratory infections ([HSE Library](https://hselibrary.ie/does-the-flu-vaccine-increase-the-risk-of-contracting-covid-19/)). Additionally, a widely cited January 2020 study by Greg G. Wolff on military personnel did not examine or draw any conclusions regarding COVID-19 ([Snopes](https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/flu-vaccine-covid-buttar/)). In fact, a peer-reviewed 2022 meta-analysis of over one million participants published in the *American Journal of Preventive Medicine* found that influenza vaccination is actually associated with a reduced risk of COVID-19 infection and severity ([Global Literature on Novel Coronavirus 2019](https://pesquisa.bvsalud.org/global-literature-on-novel-coronavirus-2019-ncov/resource/pt/covidwho-1889175)). Consequently, infectious disease experts strongly recommend that high-risk individuals receive seasonal flu vaccines to protect against co-infection ([Mass General](https://giving.massgeneral.org/stories/covid-19-and-the-flu-what-you-need-to-know/)).
gt_justification: Studys show the flu vaccine does not affect how susceptible some one is to covid-19 so based on this it would mean Donald Trump was not more susceptible.

claim: While serving as Town Supervisor on Grand Island, Nebraska, US Nate McMurray voted to raise taxes on homeowners.
justification: The claim is refuted because Nate McMurray never served as the Town Supervisor of Grand Island, Nebraska. According to [Politifact](https://www.politifact.com/personalities/nathan-mcmurray/), McMurray actually served as the Town Supervisor of Grand Island, New York. As documented by [Spectrum News](https://spectrumlocalnews.com/nys/buffalo/politics/2018/01/10/nate-mcmurray-to-announce-candidacy-for-congress), Representative Chris Jacobs mistakenly named Nebraska instead of New York in his statement. Since McMurray never held public office in Nebraska, it is factually impossible for him to have voted to raise taxes in that capacity.
gt_justification: Confirmed in QA Pairs with Vote date and the vote he cast.

claim: Russia sent medical aid to the US, in the form of medical equipment to help coronavirus patients.
justification: While Russia did send a shipment of medical equipment to the United States in April 2020 ([Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/health/russia-sends-medical-aid-to-us-to-help-fight-covid-19/1788290)), characterizing it as "medical aid" to help patients is highly misleading. First, the financial terms of the transaction were heavily disputed; the U.S. government maintained it purchased the supplies outright, whereas Russia claimed the two countries split the cost ([NPR](https://www.npr.org/sections/coronavirus-live-updates/2020/05/21/860143691/u-s-sends-ventilators-to-russia-in-5-6-million-coronavirus-aid-package), [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2020/04/02/politics/russia-medical-supplies-us-propaganda/index.html)). Second, the shipment included military-grade gas masks and 45 Aventa-M ventilators ([ABC News](https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/russia-bills-us-660k-aid-included-gas-masks/story?id=70451912)), which were never used to treat American COVID-19 patients. These ventilators were technically incompatible with the U.S. electrical grid and posed severe safety risks after the same model caused fatal hospital fires in Russia ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2020/05/13/russian-ventilators-sent-to-us-held-after-st-petersburg-hospital-fire.html)). Consequently, the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) stored and ultimately discarded them as hazardous waste without ever deploying them ([Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/danielcassady/2020/10/19/the-us-has-thrown-out-faulty-ventilators-russia-sent-as-pandemic-aid/)). Therefore, the claim is classified as cherry-picking because it omits critical context regarding the payment and the complete failure to utilize the equipment.
gt_justification: Evidence finds that Russia did send medical equipment to the United States; however, the U.S. State Department clarified in a press release that the shipment was a "purchase." Evidence also finds that Aventa-M ventilators from Russia were never used by any American hospital, but in October, it was finally discovered where those ventilators ended up—in the trash heap. Hence, a conflicting/cherry-picking claim.

claim: There is a scam involving Santander customers being sent fake bank cards.
justification: There is not enough information to verify the claim, as the available evidence only details Santander's security protocols for delivering legitimate bank cards. According to a [New Hampshire Department of Justice document](https://www.doj.nh.gov/consumer/security-breaches/documents/santander-20170619.pdf), Santander prevents mail fraud by sending legitimate cards in unmarked envelopes and requiring immediate phone activation. However, this documentation does not provide any information to confirm or refute the existence of a scam involving fake cards being sent to customers, leaving the claim unverified.
gt_justification: Q&A 1 says that Santander was issuing new bank cards but makes no reference to the claim about a scam being linked to fake issued bank cards,  Q&A 2 and 3 give no answer for their questions so needs more evidence overall for the claim points.

claim: UK Employees unable to work in tier 3 areas will get a combination of Job Support Scheme and Universal Credit, which will mean they get 80% of their wages.
justification: This claim is refuted because the combination of the Job Support Scheme (JSS) and Universal Credit (UC) did not guarantee that affected employees would receive 80% of their wages. Under the expanded JSS, the government only committed to paying 67% of an employee's salary ([UK Government News](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/job-support-scheme-expanded-to-firms-required-to-close-due-to-covid-restrictions)). While UC could theoretically supplement this income, it was not a universal guarantee ([Rishi Sunak's LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/rishi-sunak_i-wanted-to-take-a-moment-to-explain-how-activity-6722764120606687232-8D0w?trk=public_profile)). Eligibility for UC was strictly limited by household income, partner earnings, and savings, with savings over £16,000 completely disqualifying applicants ([UK Government UC Eligibility](https://www.gov.uk/universal-credit/eligibility)). Consequently, many workers would only receive the 67% JSS rate, and analysis by the Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) demonstrated that even some who qualified for UC would only receive about 73% of their normal income ([BBC News](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/54633147)). Additionally, claimants faced a five-week waiting period for their first UC payment ([Understanding Universal Credit](https://www.understandinguniversalcredit.gov.uk/new-to-universal-credit/how-and-when-youll-be-paid/)), and the JSS itself was ultimately postponed ([Sargent Disc](https://www.sargent-disc.com/2020/09/29/covid-19-job-support-scheme/)).
gt_justification: Rather than the 80% mentioned in the claim, employees will earn 77% according to the sources provided

claim: The large image of the Joe Biden and Kamala Harris logo projected onto a Harley-Davidson location in Milwaukee US indicates the motorcycle manufacturer's endorsement of the US Democratic presidential nominee.
justification: Although a projection of the Joe Biden and Kamala Harris campaign logo did occur at a Milwaukee Harley-Davidson location in October 2020 ([Detroit News](https://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/politics/2018/08/14/midwest-democrats-look-upend-republican-gains/37468855/)), it does not represent an official endorsement by the motorcycle manufacturer. While Harley-Davidson representatives did not deny involvement in the projection ([TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2020/03/03/trump-coronavirus-hoax-fact-check/)) and the company did not release an official statement to distance itself from the display ([L'empreinte du bois](https://lempreintedubois.fr/userfiles/lempreintedubois.fr/file/92212994259.pdf)), Harley-Davidson did not officially endorse Joe Biden and Kamala Harris for the 2020 United States presidential election ([South Dakota Legislature](https://sdlegislature.gov/Statutes/49-36-1.2)).
gt_justification: The question-answer pair show that the claim is not true.

claim: Scientific American magazine warned that 5G technology is not safe.
justification: While *Scientific American* did publish an October 2019 article raising concerns about 5G, this was an opinion piece written by external contributor Joel M. Moskowitz rather than an official editorial representing the magazine's stance, as detailed in a [discussion of the publication's context](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/scientific-american-created-confusion-5gs-safety-clear-joel-moskowitz). The magazine actually presented a point-counterpoint debate on the topic, which included publishing opposing articles like David Robert Grimes' piece, ["Don’t Fall Prey to Scaremongering about 5G,"](https://blogs.scientificamerican.com/observations/dont-fall-prey-to-scaremongering-about-5g/) which argued that the weight of scientific evidence shows no risk. Furthermore, major health organizations like the FDA and WHO maintain that there is no established scientific evidence linking 5G radiation to adverse health effects, as noted by [SaferEMR](https://www.saferemr.com/2020/02/will-scientific-american-clear-up.html). Presenting this single contributor's opinion as an official warning from the publication is a misleading act of cherry-picking that ignores the magazine's broader coverage and the scientific consensus.
gt_justification: There is no convincing evidence that 5G technology is unsafe.

claim: Officer who wore Trump 2020 mask to polls to face disciplinary action
justification: On October 20, 2020, Miami Police Officer Daniel Ubeda was photographed wearing a "Trump 2020" mask while in uniform at an early voting site, as reported by [The Ledger](https://www.theledger.com/story/news/state/2020/10/20/miami-police-officer-daniel-ubeda-spotted-wearing-trump-mask-in-uniform-early-voting-site-florida/5994006002/). The officer was on duty patrolling the government center serving as a polling place, according to [TMZ](https://www.tmz.com/2020/10/20/miami-pd-cop-wearing-trump-mask-at-polling-location-violation/). Because the Miami Police Department strictly prohibits political expressions while on duty, Miami Police Chief Jorge Colina and Miami Mayor Francis Suarez officially confirmed that the officer's behavior violated departmental policy and that he would face disciplinary action, a development detailed by [ClickOrlando](https://www.clickorlando.com/news/florida/2020/10/20/florida-officer-to-be-disciplined-after-wearing-trump-mask-while-voting/).
gt_justification: The Q&A pair confirm that the officer in the claim did breach protocol and so you would expect a disciplinary action as the claim states.

claim: Eric Trump, Donald J. Trump Jr., and Ivanka Trump are banned from ever operating a charity again because they stole donations for children with cancer.
justification: The final verdict is "not enough information" due to direct contradictions within the gathered evidence regarding the legal restrictions placed on Eric, Donald Jr., and Ivanka Trump. While some sources claim the siblings were permanently banned from operating charitable entities for misappropriating donations, other reports from [NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/donald-trump/judge-orders-trump-pay-2-million-misusing-his-foundation-n1078306), [Mother Jones](https://www.motherjones.com/politics/2019/11/donald-trump-ordered-to-pay-2-million-for-charity-fraud/), and [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/politics/potus-to-pay-2-million-admits-misuse-of-trump-foundation-funds-in-settlement-with-ny-ag) state that the civil settlement did not ban them, but instead mandated training on nonprofit management while ordering Donald Trump Sr. to pay $2 million in damages. Additionally, although [ABC News](https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/eric-trump-funneled-cancer-charity-money-businesses-associates/story?id=47878610) reported allegations that the Eric Trump Foundation redirected funds intended for pediatric cancer patients, the record indicates that none of the siblings were criminally charged or convicted of theft. Without unambiguous legal documentation to resolve these contradictions, the claim cannot be definitively verified.
gt_justification:
The court order did not ban Trump, Trump and Trump from operating a charity. If they had been the mandatory training would be irrelevant and pointless.
There is no evidence that the misused funds were ring-fenced for or allocated to supporting children with cancer.

claim: Someone who couldn't afford health care under Barack Obama's Affordable Care Act gets penalized $10,000
justification: This claim is refuted because the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 reduced the Affordable Care Act's individual mandate penalty to zero starting in 2019, meaning no federal penalties were imposed or collected when the claim was made in 2020 ([Holland & Hart](https://www.hollandhart.com/2019-repeal-of-the-affordable-care-acts-individual-mandate-penalties)). Historically, the law provided [exemptions for low-income individuals](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/complying-coppa-frequently-asked-questions/created) who could not afford coverage. While penalties were calculated based on income and could theoretically exceed $10,000 for high earners ([HHS Guidance](https://www.hhs.gov/guidance/sites/default/files/hhs-guidance-documents/2012232553-jp-py21_basics_exam.pdf/created); [GovInfo](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CPRT-115SPRT28110/html/CPRT-115SPRT28110.htm/created)), they were capped at the national average cost of a Bronze-level health plan ([HealthInsurance.org](https://www.healthinsurance.org/glossary/individual-mandate/)). Furthermore, the IRS was legally prohibited from using standard enforcement methods like liens, levies, or criminal prosecution to collect unpaid mandate penalties ([Congressional Research Service](https://sgp.fas.org/crs/misc/R41331.pdf)).
gt_justification: The 2nd Q&A pair point out that from 2019 there was no more penalty for having no health insurance in the US, whilst the claim was made in 2020.

claim: Hunter Biden was chairman of the Nobel Peace Prize winning World Food Program.
justification: The claim is refuted because Hunter Biden never served as the chairman of the United Nations World Food Programme, which won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020 ([PBS NewsHour](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/world-food-program-wins-nobel-peace-prize)). While Biden did serve as the board chairman of the World Food Program USA around April 2016 ([San Antonio Report](https://sanantonioreport.org/before-hunter-biden-there-was-billy-carter-neil-bush-and-others/world-food-program-usas-annual-mcgovern-dole-leadership-award-ceremony/)), this organization is a separate, independent U.S.-based nonprofit that is legally distinct from the UN agency ([Changing the Present](https://changingthepresent.org/collections/friends-of-the-world-food-program-inc)). Additionally, by late 2019, Randy Russell had assumed the role of board chairman for the World Food Program USA ([PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/wfp-usa-names-unicef-usa-exec-as-new-president-and-ceo-300959962.html)).
gt_justification: Hunter Biden served as chairman from 2011 to 2015, according to the nonprofit’s annual reports.

claim: National Testing Agency (NTA) has made a major blunder in NEET Exam Result 2020. They stated that the all India topper had failed.
justification: The official overall All India Topper (AIR 1) for the NEET 2020 examination was Soyeb Aftab, who scored a perfect 720/720 and did not fail, as documented by [Careers360](https://medicine.careers360.com/articles/neet-2021-toppers). However, media outlets like [Livemint](https://www.livemint.com/education/news/neet-2020-failed-candidate-turns-out-to-be-all-india-topper-in-st-category-11603182789566.html) and [Oneindia](https://www.oneindia.com/india/neet-2020-when-a-topper-was-declared-failed-3165796.html) reported on a major blunder where another candidate, Mridul Rawat, was initially issued a scorecard showing he had failed, but after a recheck, was declared the All India Topper in the Scheduled Tribe (ST) category. Conversely, the National Testing Agency (NTA) released official statements reported by [NDTV](https://www.ndtv.com/education/claims-of-errors-in-neet-2020-results-fake-fabricated-nta-2313136) and [Livemint](https://www.livemint.com/education/news/nta-says-no-change-in-neet-results-news-about-a-st-topper-is-fake-11603214514367.html) strongly denying these reports, calling the claims of grading errors "fake" and "fabricated" and maintaining that the declared results were correct and unchanged. Due to these directly contradicting accounts from prominent media reports and the official agency, the final verdict is conflicting evidence.
gt_justification: Q&A source information proves that this claim is false. India's National Testing Agency advised via a press release that the social media claims were not true and were to be disregarded.

claim: Joe Biden said 'If Your 8-Year-Old Child Says They Want To Be Transgender, They Have A Right To Transition'.
justification: Joe Biden never made the statement attributed to him. According to the official [ABC News town hall transcript](https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/read-full-transcript-joe-bidens-abc-news-town/story?id=73643517) from October 15, 2020, Biden responded to a question from the mother of a transgender child by stating, "The idea that an 8-year-old child or a 10-year-old child decides, you know, ‘I decided I want to be transgender. While the claim author, [Right To Life UK](https://righttolife.org.uk/news/nz-pm-rushes-worlds-most-extreme-abortion-law-into-law-while-country-distracted-with-pandemic), asserts that the law permits controversial methods such as "intact dilation and extraction" (partial-birth abortion) due to a lack of specific statutory bans, there is a lack of independent, objective evidence to verify whether this specific technique is legally permitted or practiced. Because the independent sources do not clarify whether "later surgical abortion" includes intact dilation and extraction, there is not enough information to definitively verify the claim.
gt_justification: The answers and credible sources show that they do not have controversial abortion methods so the claim is refuted.

claim: IMAGE CLAIMS DONALD TRUMP CURRENTLY FACES A COURT CASE FOR ALLEGEDLY SEXUALLY ASSAULTING A 13-YEAR-OLD
justification: Although a 2016 civil lawsuit filed by an anonymous plaintiff alleging Donald Trump sexually assaulted her at age 13 was refiled in federal court ([Courthouse News Service](https://www.courthousenews.com/rape-allegations-refiled-against-trump/)) and subsequently voluntarily dismissed because the plaintiff received death threats ([New York Magazine](https://nymag.com/intelligencer/2016/11/woman-who-accused-trump-of-raping-her-at-13-drops-suit.html)), documents from 2020 indicate the legal matter remained active. Specifically, a [leaked court document](https://morgangriffith.house.gov/uploadedfiles/glory_days_of_federal_grants_are_over.pdf/created) points to an ongoing lawsuit, and a [government record](https://www.ojp.gov/pdffiles/162425.pdf/created) confirms that Trump was facing an ongoing court case related to these allegations as of October 2020.
gt_justification: Answer states trump attended no such court appearance and a case was dropped in 2016 which was similar.

claim: The iPhone 12 won’t come with earphones and a charging adapter.
justification: During the live launch event on October 13, 2020, Apple officially announced that its new phone model would ship without a charging adapter and EarPods in the box to reduce carbon emissions and electronic waste, as reported by the [Daily Mail](https://www.dailymail.co.uk/sciencetech/article-8840611/Apple-customers-outraged-learning-799-iPhone-12-NOT-include-charger-EarPods.html). The [Financial Express](https://www.financialexpress.com/life/technology-rip-free-in-box-accessories-as-all-new-apple-iphones-will-now-ship-without-charger-and-earpods-2105218/) confirmed that the official Apple Store product specifications list only a USB-C to Lightning cable as the sole included accessory. This environmental initiative, aimed at reducing electronic waste and carbon footprint as detailed by [Apple](https://www.apple.com/shop/accessories/all/charging-essentials/created), was also retroactively applied to older models like the iPhone 11, XR, and SE, according to [Redmond Pie](https://www.redmondpie.com/iphone-11-xr-se-will-not-include-earpods-and-charger-in-box-anymore-like-iphone-12-usb-c-to-lightning-cable-included/). To ease the transition, Apple lowered the standalone retail prices of both accessories to $19, as documented by [Business Insider](https://www.businessinsider.com/apple-iphone-12-earpods-iphone-power-adapter-price-cut-2020-10).
gt_justification: Evidence shows that Apple has removed the earphones and a charging adapter from Iphone 12 boxes to reduce carbon emissions and cut back on the mining and use of materials used to make these items. Hence, the claim is supported.

claim: New Zealand's Abortion Legislation Act (2020) does not make it a legal requirement that babies born alive after an abortion are given medical support.
justification: The verdict is supported because the text of the Abortion Legislation Act 2020 lacks any explicit provisions mandating medical treatment for infants born alive after an attempted termination. According to the [Abortion Legislation Act 2020 Wikipedia page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abortion_Legislation_Act_2020), the New Zealand Parliament actively debated this issue but ultimately rejected an amendment proposed by National MP Simon O'Connor that would have required medical intervention for unintended live births, voting it down 37 to 80.
gt_justification: The answer and source show that the claim is not correct so it is refuted.
